parsed_tool.name: featureCounts
parsed_tool.description: Measure gene expression in RNA-Seq experiments from SAM or BAM files

inputs.name: alignment
inputs.label: Alignment file
inputs.help: The input alignment file(s) where the gene expression has to be counted. The file can have a SAM or BAM format; but ALL files must be in the same format. Unless you are using a Gene annotation file from the History, these files must have the database/genome attribute already specified e.g. hg38, not the default: ?

inputs.name: strand_specificity
inputs.label: Specify strand information
inputs.help: Indicate if the data is stranded and if strand-specific read counting should be performed. Strand setting must be the same as the strand settings used to produce the mapped BAM input(s)

options.label: A GFF/GTF file in your history

parameters.name: bgenome
parameters.label: Select built-in genome
parameters.help: Built-in gene annotations for genomes hg38, hg19, mm10 and mm9 are included in featureCounts

validators.message: A built-in annotation file is not available for the genome build associated with the selected input file

parameters.name: reference_gene_sets_cached
parameters.label: Using locally cached annotation
parameters.help: If the annotation file you require is not listed here, please contact the Galaxy administrator.

validators.message: A cached annotation file is not available for the genome build associated with the selected input file

parameters.name: gff_feature_type
parameters.label: GFF feature type filter
parameters.help: Specify the feature type. Only rows which have the matched matched feature type in the provided GTF annotation file will be included for read counting. `exon' by default.

parameters.name: gff_feature_attribute
parameters.label: GFF gene identifier
parameters.help: Specify the attribute type used to group features (eg. exons) into meta-features (eg. genes), when GTF annotation is provided. `gene_id' by default. This attribute type is usually the gene identifier. This argument is useful for the meta-feature level summarization. Ex: if the 9th column is 'gene_id "ENSG00000223972"; gene_name "DDX11L1" gene_source "havana"' (GTF) or 'gene_id=ENSG00000223972; gene_name=DDX11L1; gene_source=havana' (GFF), the available attributes for this feature are 'gene_id', 'gene_name' and 'gene_source'.

parameters.name: summarization_level
parameters.label: On feature level
parameters.help: If specified, read summarization will be performed at the feature level. By default (-f is not specified), the read summarization is performed at the meta-feature level.

parameters.name: reference_gene_sets
parameters.label: Gene annotation file
parameters.help: The program assumes that the provided annotation file is in GFF/GTF format. Make sure that the gene annotation file corresponds to the same reference genome as used for the alignment.

parameters.name: gff_feature_type
parameters.label: GFF feature type filter
parameters.help: Specify the feature type. Only rows which have the matched matched feature type in the provided GTF annotation file will be included for read counting. `exon' by default.

parameters.name: gff_feature_attribute
parameters.label: GFF gene identifier
parameters.help: Specify the attribute type used to group features (eg. exons) into meta-features (eg. genes), when GTF annotation is provided. `gene_id' by default. This attribute type is usually the gene identifier. This argument is useful for the meta-feature level summarization. Ex: if the 9th column is 'gene_id "ENSG00000223972"; gene_name "DDX11L1" gene_source "havana"' (GTF) or 'gene_id=ENSG00000223972; gene_name=DDX11L1; gene_source=havana' (GFF), the available attributes for this feature are 'gene_id', 'gene_name' and 'gene_source'.

parameters.name: summarization_level
parameters.label: On feature level
parameters.help: If specified, read summarization will be performed at the feature level. By default (-f is not specified), the read summarization is performed at the meta-feature level.

inputs.name: format
inputs.label: Output format
inputs.help: The output format will be tabular, select the preferred columns here

options.label: featureCounts 1.4.0+ default (includes regions provided by the GTF file)

inputs.name: include_feature_length_file
inputs.label: Create gene-length file
inputs.help: Creates a tabular file that contains the effective (nucleotides used for counting reads) length of the feature; might be useful for estimating FPKM/RPKM

test_parameter.name: paired_end_status
test_parameter.label: Does the input have read pairs?
test_parameter.help: Were the bam files generated by aligning the output of a paired-end sequencing experiment? If yes, the tool can consider 2 reads = 1 read pair as 1 entity to count. Alternatively, you can opt to consider treating the read pairs as 2 individual reads to count seperately.

options.label: Yes, paired-end but still count them as if individual reads.
Yes, paired-end and count them as 1 single fragment.

parameters.name: only_both_ends
parameters.label: Only allow fragments with both reads aligned
parameters.help: If specified, only fragments that have both ends successfully aligned will be considered for summarization. This option is only applicable for paired-end reads.

parameters.name: exclude_chimerics
parameters.label: Exclude chimeric fragments
parameters.help: If specified, the chimeric fragments (those fragments that have their two ends aligned to different chromosomes) will NOT be included for summarization. This option is only applicable for paired-end read data.

test_parameter.name: P
test_parameter.label: Check paired-end distance
test_parameter.help: If specified, paired-end distance will be checked when assigning fragments to meta-features or features. This option is only applicable when -p (Count fragments instead of reads) is specified. The distance thresholds can be specified using -d and -D (minimum and maximum fragment/template length) options.

options.label: Check the distance between paired reads

parameters.name: only_both_ends
parameters.label: Only allow fragments with both reads aligned
parameters.help: If specified, only fragments that have both ends successfully aligned will be considered for summarization. This option is only applicable for paired-end reads.

parameters.name: exclude_chimerics
parameters.label: Exclude chimeric fragments
parameters.help: If specified, the chimeric fragments (those fragments that have their two ends aligned to different chromosomes) will NOT be included for summarization. This option is only applicable for paired-end read data.

parameters.name: mapping_quality
parameters.label: Minimum mapping quality per read
parameters.help: The minimum mapping quality score a read must satisfy in order to be counted. For paired-end reads, at least one end should satisfy this criteria. 0 by default.

parameters.name: splitonly
parameters.label: Filter split alignments
parameters.help: Split alignments are alignments with CIGAR string containing 'N', e.g. exon spanning reads in RNASeq.

options.label: No filtering: count split and non-split alignments

parameters.name: primary
parameters.label: Only count primary alignments
parameters.help: If specified, only primary alignments will be counted. Primary and secondary alignments are identified using bit 0x100 in theFlag field of SAM/BAM files. All primary alignments in a dataset will be counted regardless of whether they are from multi-mapping reads or not ('-M' is ignored).

parameters.name: ignore_dup
parameters.label: Ignore reads marked as duplicate
parameters.help: If specified, reads that were marked as duplicates will be ignored. Bit Ox400 in the FLAG field of a SAM/BAM file is used for identifying duplicate reads. In paired end data, the entire read pair will be ignored if at least one end is found to be a duplicate read.

test_parameter.name: multifeat
test_parameter.label: Allow reads to map to multiple features

options.label: Disabled: reads that align to multiple features or overlapping features are excluded
Enabled: both multi-mapping and multi-overlapping features are included (-M -O)

parameters.name: fraction
parameters.label: Assign fractions to multi-mapping reads
parameters.help: If specified, a fractional count 1/x will be generated for each multi-mapping read, where x is the number of alignments (indicated by 'NH' tag) reported for the read.

parameters.name: fraction
parameters.label: Assign fractions to multi-overlapping features
parameters.help: If specified, a fractional count 1/y will be generated for each multi-overlapping feature, where y is the number of features overlapping with the read.

parameters.name: fraction
parameters.label: Assign fractions to both multi-mapping reads and multi-overlapping features
parameters.help: If specified, a fractional count 1/(x*y) will be generated, where x is the number of alignments (indicated by 'NH' tag) and y the number of overlapping features.

test_parameter.name: count_exon_exon_junction_reads
test_parameter.label: Exon-exon junctions
test_parameter.help: Junctions are identified from those exon-spanning reads (containing ‘N’ in CIGAR string) in input data. The output result includes names of primary and secondary genes that overlap at least one of the two splice sites of a junction.

options.label: Count reads supporting each exon-exon junction.

parameters.name: genome
parameters.label: Reference sequence file
parameters.help: The FASTA-format file that contains the reference sequences used in read mapping can be used to improve read counting for junctions

parameters.name: long_reads
parameters.label: Long reads
parameters.help: If specified, long reads such as Nanopore and PacBio reads will be counted. Long read counting can only run in one thread and only reads (not read-pairs) can be counted.

parameters.name: by_read_group
parameters.label: Count reads by read group
parameters.help: If specified, reads are counted for each read group separately. The 'RG' tag must be present in the input BAM/SAM alignment files.

parameters.name: largest_overlap
parameters.label: Largest overlap
parameters.help: If specified, reads (or fragments) will be assigned to the target that has the largest number of overlapping bases

parameters.name: min_overlap
parameters.label: Minimum bases of overlap
parameters.help: Specify the minimum required number of overlapping bases between a read (or a fragment) and a feature. 1 by default. If a negative value is provided, the read will be extended from both ends.

parameters.name: frac_overlap
parameters.label: Minimum fraction (of read) overlapping a feature
parameters.help: Specify the minimum required fraction of overlapping bases between a read (or a fragment) and a feature. Value should be within range [0,1]. 0 by default. Number of overlapping bases is counted from both reads if paired end. Both this option and '--minOverlap' need to be satisfied for read assignment.

parameters.name: frac_overlap_feature
parameters.label: Minimum fraction (of feature) overlapping a read
parameters.help: Specify the minimum required fraction of bases included in a feature overlapping bases between a read (or a read-pair). Value should be within range [0,1]. 0 by default.

parameters.name: read_extension_5p
parameters.label: Read 5' extension
parameters.help: Reads are extended upstream by ... bases from their 5' end

parameters.name: read_extension_3p
parameters.label: Read 3' extension
parameters.help: Reads are extended upstream by ... bases from their 3' end

parameters.name: read_reduction
parameters.label: Reduce read to single position
parameters.help: The read is reduced to its 5' most base or 3'most base. Read summarization is then performed based on the single base the the read is reduced to.

options.label: Leave the read as it is

parameters.name: R
parameters.label: Annotates the alignment file with 'XS:Z:'-tags to described per read or read-pair the corresponding assigned feature(s).

help.content:
featureCounts
#############

Overview
--------
FeatureCounts is a light-weight read counting program written entirely in the C programming language. It can be used to count both gDNA-seq and RNA-seq reads for genomic features in in SAM/BAM files. FeatureCounts is part of the Subread_ package.

Input formats
-------------
Alignments should be provided in either:

 - SAM format, http://samtools.sourceforge.net/samtools.shtml#5
 - BAM format

Annotations for gene regions should be provided in the GFF/GTF format:

 - http://genome.ucsc.edu/FAQ/FAQformat.html#format3
 - http://www.ensembl.org/info/website/upload/gff.html

Alternatively, the featureCounts built-in annotations for genomes hg38, hg19, mm10 and mm9 can be used through selecting the built-in option above. These annotation files are in simplified annotation format (SAF) as shown below. The GeneID column contains Entrez gene identifiers and each entry (row) is taken as a feature (e.g. an exon).

Example - **Built-in annotation format**:

  ======  ====  =======  =======  ======
  GeneID  Chr   Start    End      Strand
  ======  ====  =======  =======  ======
  497097  chr1  3204563  3207049  -
  497098  chr1  3411783  3411982  -
  497099  chr1  3660633  3661579  -
  ======  ====  =======  =======  ======

These annotation files can be found in the _`Subread package`_. You can see the version of Subread used by this wrapper in the tool form above under `Options > Requirements`. To create the files, the annotations were downloaded from NCBI RefSeq database and then adapted by merging overlapping exons from the same gene to form a set of disjoint exons for each gene. Genes with the same Entrez gene identifiers were also merged into one gene. See the `Subread User's Guide`_ for more information. Gene names can be obtained for these Entrez identifiers with the Galaxy **annotateMyIDs** tool.

Output format
-------------
FeatureCounts produces a table containing counted reads, per gene, per row. Optionally the last column can be set to be the effective gene-length. These tables are compatible with the DESeq2, edgeR and limma-voom Galaxy wrappers by IUC.

.. _Subread: http://subread.sourceforge.net/
.. _`Subread User's Guide`: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/Rsubread/inst/doc/SubreadUsersGuide.pdf
